title: Hover-to-select on the Detect tool + a COCO YOLO model
description:
Replaces MPI-361 Phase B (SAM3 text masking), cancelled 2026-07-29. The user's objection to text was that selection should be DISCOVERED, not described: hover an object, see it highlight, click it. SAM3 cannot do that - it is strictly prompt-driven and the engine has no automatic-mask-generation node at all (both proven live, see MPI-361 validation.md). YOLO can, because it enumerates objects without being told what to look for.

TWO PARTS, deliberately separable - part 1 ships value with no download at all.

PART 1 - HOVER-TO-SELECT over the detections we ALREADY have.
A Detect run already produces per-object regions; today the user picks them from the thumb strip. Move the interaction onto the image: hovering a detected region highlights it (a seg model can show the mask outline, a bbox-only model shows the box), clicking selects it, which is the same act as clicking its thumb. The thumb strip STAYS - it is the readout of what was found and the multi-pick surface. This is a UI layer over data already in the viewer, so no new node, no new model, no download, no workflow change.

PART 2 - a COCO YOLO model so the detector covers everyday objects.
Today the Detect vocabulary is 4 entries (face / hair / hand / person). Add a COCO-trained YOLO for the 80 common classes (person, cat, dog, chair, bottle, tv, car...). PREFER THE -seg VARIANT (yolov8n-seg.pt, ~7MB) over plain yolov8n.pt: segmentation masks make the hover highlight a real object outline instead of a rectangle, which is the whole point of part 1.

HOW DETECTORS ARE DECLARED (verified, do not invent a new mechanism): js/data/modelConstants/assetDeps.js, alongside 'face-yolov8n' / 'hand-yolov8n' / 'person-yolov8n-seg'. Shape = { id, name, filename: 'ultralytics/bbox/<file>', url: 'https://models.cubric.studio/vision/models/ultralytics/bbox/<file>', size, sha256, engineAsset: true }. They are engineAssets - boot-installed when missing and self-healing after a node re-clone - NOT per-model deps, so nothing GCs them. The file must be uploaded to R2 first (see MadPony-Identity/capabilities/cloudflare-r2/README.md; rclone needs --s3-no-check-bucket or a scoped token 403s on CreateBucket, and NEVER pipe rclone to tail - $? becomes tail's).

The UI list is DETECTION_MODELS in MpiCanvasViewer.js, surfaced by el.getDetectionModels() so the options compounds do not fork it. MpiToolOptionsMaskDetect renders the radios. A COCO model has 80 classes rather than one, so decide how it presents - a single 'Objects' entry that detects everything it can, most likely, rather than 80 radio buttons.

OPEN QUESTION for part 2, settle before wiring: the existing 4 entries are one-class detectors where the radio IS the class. A COCO model detects many classes at once. Does it become one more radio ('Objects'), or does it change the shape of that control? Do not guess.

--- BRAINSTORM OUTCOME 2026-07-29 (supersedes the guesses above where they conflict) ---

PROVEN LIVE on our own 0.28.0 engine, see MPI-380 brief.md for the full record:
1. THE ENUMERATOR IS yolov8n-seg IN ultralytics/segm/, NOT bbox/. Impact Pack decides bbox vs segm by FOLDER, not filename - the same file in bbox/ crashes with a NO_SEGM_DETECTOR error. From segm/ it returns native masks in 0.5s, FASTER than box mode (0.8s) and flat regardless of object count.
2. HOVER CAN NAME WHAT IT IS. ImpactDecomposeSEGS -> ImpactFrom_SEG_ELT (output slot 7 = label) -> returns per-region class strings. That settles the readout question: the thumb strip is not needed as an index, because hover says the word.
3. CLASS FILTERING IS THE labels STRING ONLY. ImpactSEGSLabelFilter.preset does NOTHING server-side (verified: preset=person + empty labels filters to zero). 106 presets exist including all 80 COCO classes; labels takes a comma list like person,dog. Inject labels, never preset.
4. NATIVE SEGM IS BLOBBY - face profile collapses, hand becomes a mitten, edges stair-step. Fine as a transient hover highlight, NOT as a committed mask. Hence the hybrid below.

USER-DECIDED INTERACTION (2026-07-29):
- Detect run returns ALL regions via native segm. Hover highlights the blob under the cursor and names it. Click refines THAT region into a real mask (MPI-380 supplies the refiner) and selects it; click again deselects.
- The blob must go green on the SAME FRAME as the click; the refined mask swaps in when it lands. Never block the click on a round trip.
- THUMB STRIP IS DROPPED. Selection happens on the canvas. The little preview box goes away on the points tool too.
- DETECT BUTTON IS DROPPED. Detection fires when the user changes model or box/segment; points detection fires when a point is added or removed. Both need a debounce.
- BOX BECOMES A CLIENT-SIDE TOGGLE over the segment (derive the bbox from mask extents in JS) instead of a second workflow run. Caveat: bbox-only detectors (face_yolov8n, hand_yolov8n) have NO native segment, so for those the box IS the preview and the refine step is what produces an outline.

DEPENDS ON MPI-380 for the click-to-refine step. Part 1 hover can be built against the existing SAM 1 refiner if MPI-380 slips.

--- STRONG CANDIDATE 2026-07-29 (user, up for debate - settle at implementation) ---

SHOW A BOX ON HOVER, NOT THE BLOB. The user saw SAM3 draw red boxes over two faces and made the point: a blobby mask under the cursor reads as POOR QUALITY, and a user who sees it may conclude the tool is bad and walk away - even though the blob is only a preview and the committed mask would be crisp. A rectangle reads as A SELECTION, not as an output, so it makes no quality promise it cannot keep. The only mask the user ever SEES would then be the refined one.

This SIMPLIFIES the build rather than complicating it:
- No per-pixel index map (the Uint8 W*H region map) is needed. Hover becomes a rectangle hit test over N boxes, smallest-area-wins for nesting.
- The enumerator may not need to be a -seg model at all, since only boxes get displayed. That would drop the segm-folder requirement and possibly the whole native-segm question.
- The coarse mask still exists behind the scenes to give the instant green on click; it is just never the hover affordance.

Open sub-question: with boxes-only, the instant green on click has to come from somewhere - either the coarse mask (kept, just not displayed on hover) or the box rectangle itself filled, upgraded when the real mask lands.

--- LATE CANDIDATE 2026-07-29: PART 2 (COCO YOLO) MAY NOT BE NEEDED AT ALL ---

Live testing showed SAM3 detects face, head, hand, person and effectively any nameable part, cleanly, from plain text (measured this session, see MPI-380 brief.md). That REPLACES the fixed detector vocabulary: our four YOLO detectors collapse into four strings, with no per-class weights, no -seg variants and no bbox-vs-segm folder trap.

Consequence for this card: PART 2 (add a COCO YOLO model for 80 everyday classes) may be unnecessary. Every flow the user has actually demonstrated is a NAMED one - pick a type, see boxes, click one. If the type buttons INJECT the word (the user proposed exactly this: a button labelled Persons that adds that text to the prompt) then nothing is ever typed, selection is still DISCOVERED by clicking rather than described, and the original objection that killed MPI-361 Phase B does not apply.

What COCO would still buy: the enumerate-everything-without-naming-it case, i.e. a generic Objects bucket. That gap is real and measured - SAM3 costs about 3.6s PER CATEGORY while YOLO returns all 80 classes in 0.5s, and an Animals bucket as SAM3 text would be roughly 10 categories at 15-20s. So buckets do NOT rescue SAM3 here.

NOT a user decision - this is an open engineering question raised by the measurements, recorded so it is not forgotten. DECIDE AT IMPLEMENTATION, do not assume: is a generic Objects bucket worth a second detection engine (a COCO model, its own R2 upload, its own folder trap and its own coarse-mask quality problem), or do named buttons plus a free-text field cover what users actually do? If the answer is named-only, Part 2 disappears and this card shrinks to hover-plus-click over SAM3 text detections.

--- UMBRELLA MPI-424, MOVED TO DOING 2026-08-01: BRAINSTORM BEFORE ANY CODE ---
This card is step 1 of the MPI-424 canvas-tool umbrella (MPI-379 -> 421 -> 382 -> 368 -> 375 -> 373) and it is in doing for a BRAINSTORM SESSION WITH THE USER, not for implementation. The user's position 2026-08-01: what they actually want is A LOT SIMPLER than what this card proposes. Everything above from 'STRONG CANDIDATE' onward is a parked option, and the card also carries an open box-vs-blob question, a possible second detection engine (COCO YOLO) and a per-pixel index map that the box option would delete outright. Do not implement any of it. Run the session, take the user's simpler model as the spec, then REWRITE this card to it and DELETE what the session rules out - do not demote it to another candidate. Agenda: tasks/MPI-424/brief.md.
acceptance: DEPENDS ON MPI-380 (SAM3 refiner). Hover itself can ship against the existing SAM 1 refiner if MPI-380 slips - do not hard-block on it
PART 1: hovering a detected region highlights it on the IMAGE and names its class; clicking selects it, clicking again deselects
PART 1: the click goes green INSTANTLY from the coarse mask, then upgrades in place when the refined mask returns. A click that waits on a round trip is a defect
PART 1: refined regions are cached per region index so deselect-then-reselect costs nothing, and the cache is dropped on the next detect run
PART 1: concurrent clicks are lane-keyed by region index so out-of-order returns cannot paint the wrong mask (this class of bug bit float-latent before)
PART 1: clicking while the Cue is busy keeps the coarse selection and upgrades quietly when the queue drains - it must NOT toast on every click
PART 1: overlapping regions resolve by smallest-area-wins, or person will eat every click once COCO is in
PART 1: hover does no work before a detection run, and never fights the brush
The Detect button and the thumb strip are GONE from both the detect and points tools; detection auto-runs on control change / point edit, debounced
Box is a client-side toggle derived from the segment - no second workflow run. Bbox-only detectors (face, hand) are handled explicitly, not left to crash
PART 2: COCO yolov8n-seg uploaded to R2 and declared as an engineAsset. It MUST be placed under ultralytics/segm/, not bbox/ - the wrong folder is a hard crash
PART 2: sha256 + byte size recorded and verified after upload

PART 2: USER DECISION STILL OPEN - a COCO model detects 80 classes at once while the existing radios are one-class-each. Does Objects become one more radio that keeps everything, or does picking it reveal a class filter (the labels string) so it can be narrowed to dog,chair?
The existing detectors and the Points tool are unaffected - regression-check Face and Person
Whatever ships is added to docs/masking.md (200-line cap, currently AT it - trim first)
